item.title: Notchkit 1.0.6
item.description:
What's new

A smoother notch, especially on MacBooks with a real notch.

  • Crisp edges at rest: on a real notch, Notchkit no longer draws its own shape over the hardware notch when nothing is happening, so the edges stay perfectly sharp.
  • Centered while opening: widgets stay centered as the notch opens, including with the Bouncy animation, and no longer shift by a couple of points at the end.
  • Live activities come back like they start: when the notch closes, it first returns to its resting size, then the live activity grows back out on each side.
  • No more accidental reopening: after the notch closes, only the closed notch area reopens it, and it waits a moment first. Moving the pointer up to the menu bar no longer reopens it by mistake.

Installation

Notchkit 1.0.3 or later offers this update by itself (or use Check for Updates… in its menu).

If you have Notchkit 1.0.2 or earlier, download Notchkit-1.0.6.dmg, open it, and drag Notchkit.app onto the Applications shortcut. Notchkit isn't notarized: the first time, right-click the app > Open. Coming from 1.0.0 or earlier, also give it the Accessibility permission again: open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility, remove Notchkit with −, then add it again.

Requires macOS 14 or later, on Apple silicon or Intel.

item.title: Notchkit 1.0.5
item.description:
What's new

  • Time left until fully charged: the Battery widget now shows when your Mac will be full ("Full at 17:40"), and the mini widget shows the time left in small type while charging, even when stacked.
  • Charging live activity (optional): turn on Time left until fully charged, while charging in Settings > Battery to see the battery gauge and the time left next to the notch while your Mac charges. It disappears once the battery is full or charging is paused.

The estimate comes from macOS, so it may take a minute to appear after you plug in.

item.title: Notchkit 1.0.4
item.description:
What's new

  • Choose the video resolution: after you paste a link, the Videos widget lists every resolution the video offers, from 144p to 4K. Pick one to download it.
  • Videos that play everywhere: downloads are now MP4 files that QuickTime opens on every Mac. Up to 1080p they use H.264. Above that, YouTube only offers AV1 or VP9, so Notchkit converts them to HEVC with your Mac's hardware encoder, with the progress shown in the notch.
  • Clearer message when ffmpeg is missing: most YouTube videos keep picture and sound separate and need ffmpeg to combine them. Notchkit now says so instead of showing yt-dlp's raw error. Install it in Terminal with brew install ffmpeg deno.
  • Thinner bubble outline: the outline of the small bubbles next to the notch is now as thin as the notch's own.

Installation

Notchkit 1.0.3 offers this update by itself (or use Check for Updates… in its menu).

If you have Notchkit 1.0.2 or earlier, download Notchkit-1.0.4.dmg, open it, and drag Notchkit.app onto the Applications shortcut. Notchkit isn't notarized: the first time, right-click the app > Open. Coming from 1.0.0 or earlier, also give it the Accessibility permission again: open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility, remove Notchkit with −, then add it again.

Requires macOS 14 or later, on Apple silicon or Intel.

item.title: Notchkit 1.0.3
item.description:
Fixed

  • Notchkit 1.0.1 and 1.0.2 didn't launch. Both versions quit right away on every Mac because of a signing issue. Sorry about that! Notchkit 1.0.3 fixes it and includes everything from 1.0.2:
  • New music player that looks like an iPhone Live Activity.
  • Pure black widgets, without a border.
  • Paused music stays in the notch, even in a browser such as Brave.
  • Smaller live activities and a smoother shadow under the expanded notch.

Installation

Because 1.0.1 and 1.0.2 couldn't launch, they can't update themselves. Download Notchkit-1.0.3.dmg, open it, and drag Notchkit.app onto the Applications shortcut, replacing the old version. Notchkit isn't notarized: the first time, right-click the app > Open.

If you're updating from Notchkit 1.0.0 or earlier, also give it the Accessibility permission again: open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility, remove Notchkit with −, then add it again. Later updates install automatically and keep the permission.

Requires macOS 14 or later, on Apple silicon or Intel.

item.title: Notchkit 1.0.2
item.description:
What's new

  • New music player: the expanded player now looks like an iPhone Live Activity, with a bold title, a thin progress bar and large white playback controls.
  • Pure black widgets: widget cards are now pure black, without a border, so they blend into the notch. Turn on Increase Contrast in System Settings > Accessibility > Display to keep a border.
  • Paused music stays in the notch: when a browser such as Brave pauses, the track now stays in the notch instead of disappearing. Press play to bring the browser to the front and resume.
  • Smaller live activities: each compact activity only takes the room its content needs. Music now uses about half the width it did.
  • Smoother shadow: the shadow under the expanded notch no longer ends in a hard line.

Installation

Notchkit 1.0.1 offers this update by itself (or use Check for Updates… in its menu), and keeps the Accessibility permission.

If you still have Notchkit 1.0.0 or earlier, it can't install this update by itself: download Notchkit-1.0.2.dmg, open it, and drag Notchkit.app onto the Applications shortcut. Notchkit isn't notarized: the first time, right-click the app > Open. Then give it the Accessibility permission again: open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility, remove Notchkit with −, then add it again.

Requires macOS 14 or later, on Apple silicon or Intel.

item.title: Notchkit 1.0.1
item.description:
What's new

  • Exact notch height: on MacBooks with a notch, Notchkit now lines up with the bottom of the physical notch instead of stopping 1 pt above it.
  • Menus stay visible: around a real notch, the compact activity no longer covers the menus of the app you're using. It shrinks to the free space, or hides while there is no room (it still opens on hover). Requires the Accessibility permission.
  • Settings icons: wide symbols such as Battery and Translation no longer overflow their tile, and all icons have a consistent size.

Please reinstall manually this once

Notchkit 1.0.1 is signed with new keys, so earlier versions can't install it by themselves: they only show a link to this page. Download Notchkit-1.0.1.dmg, open it, and drag Notchkit.app onto the Applications shortcut, replacing the old version. Notchkit isn't notarized: the first time, right-click the app > Open.

macOS will also need the Accessibility permission again: open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility, remove Notchkit with −, then add it again. Later updates install automatically again and keep the permission.

Requires macOS 14 or later, on Apple silicon or Intel.

item.title: Notchkit 1.0.0
item.description:
Notchkit 1.0

The biggest update yet: 17 new widgets and features, all free and running on your Mac. New widgets are off by default: turn on the ones you like in Settings.

What's new

  • Quick Toggles: Dark Mode, stay awake, hide desktop icons, and a keyboard lock to clean it.
  • Webcam: a quick mirror to check how you look before a meeting.
  • System Monitor: CPU per core, GPU, memory, disk, network speed, battery health, and heavy processes.
  • Dashboard: your favorite apps and your Mac at a glance.
  • Window Snapping: drag a window toward the notch and drop it on a half, third, quarter or full screen.
  • Live Activities: stopwatch, alarms and Pomodoro (25 min focus, 5 min break), on top of timers.
  • Reminders: check off and add reminders from the notch.
  • Notes: a scratchpad one hover away.
  • Day progress: how far along your workday you are (8:00 to 18:00 by default).
  • Screen Time and Health: time spent per app, break and hydration reminders, and activity rings, measured on your Mac only.
  • Translation: French ↔ English on device (macOS 15 or later).
  • Git: branch and changes of the project open in Xcode or Terminal, with fetch and pull.
  • GitHub: your pull requests and their checks, with a personal access token kept in the keychain.
  • Ollama: the models your local AI server has loaded.
  • Shelf: drop text as well as files, then compress, convert images and videos, or copy them to iCloud Drive.
  • Settings: modules grouped by category, and a Copy Diagnostic Information item in the menu.

Known issue on macOS 27

On some Macs running macOS 27 Golden Gate, the notch may not appear. If that happens to you, choose Copy Diagnostic Information in the Notchkit menu and paste it into a new issue: it helps fix it quickly.

Installation

Notchkit 0.1.5 or later offers this update by itself (or use Check for Updates… in its menu).

Otherwise, download Notchkit-1.0.0.dmg, open it, and drag Notchkit.app onto the Applications shortcut. Notchkit isn't notarized: the first time, right-click the app > Open.

Requires macOS 14 or later, on Apple silicon or Intel.

item.title: Notchkit 0.1.9
item.description:
What's new

  • Screenshots widget: the screenshots and screen recordings you made since your Mac started or you logged in, wherever they are saved. Drag them into any app, open, copy, send with AirDrop or move them to the Trash. A small alert appears in the notch for each new screenshot.
  • Shelf without the widget: files dropped on the notch are kept even if the Shelf widget is hidden.
  • Widgets that show up when needed: the Shelf and Screenshots widgets appear by themselves as an extra page while they have something to show, without changing your layout. Right-click one and choose Add to Layout to keep it for good.
  • Permissions kept across updates: Notchkit is now signed with a stable certificate, so macOS keeps its permissions (like Accessibility) from one version to the next.

Installation

Notchkit 0.1.5 or later offers this update by itself (or use Check for Updates… in its menu).

Otherwise, download Notchkit-0.1.9.dmg, open it, and drag Notchkit.app onto the Applications shortcut. Notchkit isn't notarized: the first time, right-click the app > Open.

One last time after this update, macOS may need the Accessibility permission again (used for the volume and brightness keys): open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility, remove Notchkit with −, then add it again. Future updates keep it.

Requires macOS 14 or later, on Apple silicon or Intel.

item.title: Notchkit 0.1.8
item.description:
What's new

  • Volume indicator with the Touch Bar: changing the volume from the Touch Bar, Control Center or another app now shows the indicator in the notch, not only the keyboard volume keys.
  • Fewer background processes: the helper that reads what's playing no longer keeps running after Notchkit quits unexpectedly, and leftovers from earlier versions are cleaned up at launch.

Installation

Notchkit 0.1.5 or later offers this update by itself (or use Check for Updates… in its menu).

Otherwise, download Notchkit-0.1.8.dmg, open it, and drag Notchkit.app onto the Applications shortcut. Notchkit isn't notarized yet: the first time, right-click the app > Open.

After updating, macOS may ask again for the Accessibility permission (used for the volume and brightness keys): if the volume indicator doesn't appear, open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility, remove Notchkit with −, then add it again.

Requires macOS 14 or later, on Apple silicon or Intel.

item.title: Notchkit 0.1.7
item.description:
What's new

Notchkit 0.1.7 is the first official release: it is no longer a beta.

  • Lock screen: the notch now stays visible on the lock screen and shows live activities in their collapsed form. It never expands while the Mac is locked.
  • New battery icon: redrawn in the style of Apple's battery icon, with a cut-out charging bolt.
  • Layout settings: hidden widgets now wrap onto several lines instead of being squeezed into one.
  • Claude Code: replying to Claude from the notch after each answer is now off by default. You can turn it on in Settings > Claude Code.

Installation

If you already have Notchkit 0.1.5 or later, it offers this update by itself (or use Check for Updates… in its menu).

Otherwise, download Notchkit-0.1.7.dmg, open it, and drag Notchkit.app onto the Applications shortcut. Notchkit isn't notarized yet: the first time, right-click the app > Open.

Requires macOS 14 or later, on Apple silicon or Intel.

item.title: Notchkit 0.1.5
item.description:
What's new

  • Automatic updates: Notchkit now checks for a new version once a day and installs it with your approval. You can also use Check for Updates… in its menu, or turn automatic checks off in Settings > General. This is the last version you need to download by hand.
  • New app icon: a Mac screen with a vivid wallpaper and the notch.

Installation

Download Notchkit-0.1.5.dmg, open it, and drag Notchkit.app onto the Applications shortcut. Notchkit isn't notarized yet: the first time, right-click the app > Open.

Requires macOS 14 or later, on Apple silicon or Intel.
